description: A Strategic Management Journal study challenges the assumption that AI adoption automatically reduces demand for managers. Liudmila Alekseeva, José Azar, Mireia Giné and Sampsa Samila analyze U.S. job postings from 2010 to 2022, linking firm-level AI adoption with managerial vacancies and skill requirements.
title: New research finds AI adoption is associated with more managers—and different managerial skills

description: A study by the University of Córdoba (UCO) departments of Forest Engineering and of Botany, Ecology and Plant Physiology reveals that the presence of invasive plants in Sierra Nevada and the Sierra de los Filabres—two mountain ecosystems in Andalusia that are especially vulnerable to climate change and home to unique plant species—is currently low. Specifically, invasive plants are most common in the areas closest to the edges of roads, and their presence declines at the highest points of the mountains.
title: Invasive plants show limited spread in Andalusia's mountains

description: At the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, a key question for negotiators is how to get more money to developing countries so they can adapt to a warming world. For the past 30 years, climate talks focused on cutting greenhouse gas emissions and preventing future global warming.
title: COP31: How to make carbon markets more effective

description: In recent years, public discussion has focused on the increasingly conservative values of young men. A recently published study indicates that this is primarily a phenomenon prominent in social and conventional media, not an overall trend.
title: Gender differences in values are not widening in Europe after all

description: Canadians are eating out less. A 2025 survey found 57% of them are cooking at home more often to save money, while 69% of restaurant operators say customers are dining out less because of affordability. According to Restaurants Canada, 41% of operators are either losing money or breaking even.
title: How restaurants can make sustainable dining choices easier while still making a profit

description: In the twelfth century, the English-speaking world underwent a major change: Old English gave way to Middle English. In his dissertation, Ph.D. candidate Amos van Baalen uses sermons to reconstruct how this change took place.
title: Writing as it should be or as it sounds: Reconstructing how Old English disappeared

description: Current CO₂ emissions covered by the EU Emissions Trading System (EU-ETS1) could be substantially reduced by 2040. A new study by the Oeko-Institut, commissioned by Carbon Market Watch, examines the level of emissions that could remain in 2040 and 2050. In 2040, installations covered by the EU-ETS1—including waste incineration—could still emit between 159 and 231 million metric tons of CO₂.
title: How much CO₂ will stay? New study estimates long-term residual emissions under the EU Emissions Trading System

description: Dogs have been living side by side with humans for millennia, but a new study underscores how much we have yet to learn about man's best friend. The study, which looked at hundreds of dogs across four nations, found that the lifestyles of pet owners appear to play a significant role in determining what constitutes a healthy gut microbiome for their dog companions.
title: How do human lifestyles affect the gut microbiome of our canine companions?

description: A new machine learning tool developed through the Centre for Resilience in Environment, Water and Waste (CREWW) could help water companies identify properties most likely to be connected to lead service pipes.
title: How machine learning can tackle lead pipe challenges

description: Can a solution that cuts food waste in Tokyo work in Seoul too? Exploring a familiar problem with peers abroad can help students question what they take for granted at home and see how their knowledge might apply to real-world sustainability challenges. As educators put time and care into designing international courses, what do students take away from the experience, and what stays with them after the course ends?
title: Study tracks what students learn from online teamwork and fieldwork abroad

description: In 2024, researchers at the Ultracold Quantum Gases group at ICFO built a quantum-gas microscope capable of imaging individual atoms in strontium quantum gases for the first time, marking a key enabling step for quantum simulation. At that time, the researchers imaged strontium-84, a boson that has no spin.
title: Quantum-gas microscope resolves the 'color' of individual atoms in a single shot

description: Much of the concern about elevated levels of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere focuses on its effects on global warming as a greenhouse gas. But up to 30% of emitted carbon dioxide is absorbed by the oceans, where it reacts with water to lower pH and leads to ocean acidification, which has enormous effects on the chemistry and biology of marine ecosystems.
title: At base of ocean food chain, scientists uncover impacts of a changing atmosphere

description: If you're reading this, then your media feed, like mine, is probably full of cats.
title: The 12th‑century Chinese poet who was among the first to explore the inner lives of cats

description: Imagine a group of newcomers in your local area. Would you expect your neighbors to welcome them or react with reluctance? Would it make a difference how many men and women were in the group, or whether they appeared white or nonwhite?
title: More than meets the eye: Refugee reception in eastern Germany can vary by group composition

description: Researchers at the FAMU-FSU College of Engineering have developed a gel that delivers therapeutic particles to injured spinal cord cells, a potential step toward new treatments for spinal cord injuries.
title: Engineered gel controls particle release to help injured spinal cord cells recover in lab

description: Insects can convert food waste and by-products from the food industry (such as unsold ready meals or slaughter by-products) into ingredients for animal feed. In this way, they can contribute to the transition toward a circular food production system, in which what would otherwise be wasted is reused. However, these waste streams may contain animal proteins that pose a risk of transmitting diseases such as bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE), also known as mad cow disease. For this reason, rearing insects on waste streams containing animal proteins is not permitted in the European Union.
title: Turning food waste into insect feed poses only low mad cow disease risk

description: A year before the Deepwater Horizon spill, a NOAA crew scooped up seawater from the Gulf and froze it. Sixteen years later, FIU biologist Shen Jean Lim tested it only to discover the microbes that devoured much of the oil in 2010 were nowhere to be found in 2009. So where did they come from?
title: The Gulf's oil-eating microbes lay in wait before Deepwater Horizon spill, frozen samples suggest

description: From tracking how cancer develops to exploring how the brain works, scientists need ways to observe biological processes at increasingly smaller scales. Beyond tracking how cells move and interact, researchers need to understand how tiny structures within cells, including organelles and molecular complexes, behave and change over time. However, identifying and tracking these microscopic targets individually remains a major challenge.
title: Lasers near physical limits of miniaturization open possibilities for tracking life at the nanoscale

description: Researchers from Chile's Institute of Ecology and Biodiversity (IEB) have developed a multiobjective model to identify priority areas for large-scale ecological restoration in Chile, South America. The tool integrates four ecological objectives: reducing species extinction risk, prioritizing carbon stocks, restoring riparian areas and assessing ecological feasibility. The findings show that including ecological feasibility changes restoration priorities, while 80.4% of the selected areas contribute to more than one ecological objective. By identifying areas where different priorities overlap, the model can help guide strategic restoration planning and support better-informed conservation decisions amid growing environmental challenges and limited resources.
title: New model identifies priority areas for large-scale ecological restoration in Chile

description: Te Whare Wānanga o Waitaha | University of Canterbury (UC) botanist professor Pieter Pelser has been recognized with one of the highest honors in taxonomy, with a newly established South American daisy genus named Pelseria in acknowledgment of his decades-long contribution to studying the family tree of plants.
title: New daisy genus named after botanist

description: In the lush mountain rainforests of Indonesia, researchers have identified a new species of Asian flying frog with distinctive physical features, calls and unusual egg-laying habits. The discovery is described in a paper published in the journal Zootaxa by scientists from Museum Zoologicum Bogoriense in Indonesia, the University of California, Davis, and other collaborators.
title: New Asian flying frog species identified in Indonesia

description: Passion fruit can travel thousands of kilometers before it reaches international markets. Along the way, one of the food industry's biggest challenges is making sure its nutritional qualities survive processing, storage and transport.
title: Extreme cold preserves passion fruit's vitamin C, but not all of its antioxidants

description: A Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL)-led team has harnessed the power of El Capitan to accelerate generation of predicted protein structures, drastically reducing the computing time required and opening new possibilities for drug discovery, biological research and national security applications.
title: Optimized supercomputer workflow accelerates protein-structure prediction

description: The process of producing essential medicines and fine chemicals has long been powered by reactions involving intense heat, heavy-metal catalysts and hazardous hydrogen gas. Now, a team of Harvard chemists and engineers has demonstrated that these critical transformations can be driven cleanly by electricity, right at the boundary where oil and water meet.
title: Repurposed battery molecules drive key chemical reactions where oil meets water

description: A new study has identified Arabidopsis SNARE proteins VAMP726 and VAMP725 as key components of the trafficking of cellulose synthase (CESA), helping support the formation of both primary and secondary cell walls.
title: Two proteins key to cellulose synthase trafficking and cell wall formation identified

description: The open-source platform, called UMIche (pronounced "you-me-kay"), is described in a new study published in Nature Communications. It addresses a common challenge in RNA-sequencing, where errors during sequencing can lead to inaccurate measurements of gene expression.
title: New platform improves accuracy of molecular counting in RNA-sequencing

description: As rainforests around the world are cleared for agriculture, livestock grazing, timber harvesting and development, habitat loss is pushing an increasing number of species toward extinction.
title: Gut microbiomes of endangered primates reveal hidden toll of habitat loss

description: Between 1970 and 2019, tropical cyclones killed nearly 780,000 people worldwide and caused approximately $1.4 trillion in economic losses. As coastal populations continue to grow and climate continues to change, accurate forecasting is essential for saving lives and reducing economic damage.
title: Rapid-scan satellite data offer clues to typhoon intensity

description: Grand Theft Auto V is one of the world's best-known video games. It is set in Los Santos, and although the city is fictional, its landscape and urban structure are modeled very closely on the American city of Los Angeles. Researchers from the Alfred Wegener Institute and the University of Potsdam have explored whether this virtual representation is detailed enough to realistically depict the consequences of a potential rise in sea levels and make them approachable.
title: GTA V flood simulations reveal how rising seas could reshape Los Santos

description: A research team from the South China Botanical Garden (SCBG) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences has uncovered a molecular regulatory mechanism that contributes to the development of curved floral organs associated with the distinctive lips of orchids, offering new insights into the development and evolution of floral forms in orchids. The study was published in New Phytologist on Nov. 6.
title: Study uncovers molecular mechanism underlying lip-related floral organ curvature in slipper orchids

description: Much of the news coverage on young men recently has focused on social media, gambling and the online "manosphere." But some of the most consequential changes in young men's lives are happening in school and workplaces.
title: International Men's Day: Young men are struggling—but not all men are struggling equally

description: Antimicrobial resistance represents one of the major challenges facing modern medicine. Especially worrying are bacteria that develop resistance to antibiotics that are the last available treatment options.
title: Newly identified cell wall mechanism may help staph resist a last-resort antibiotic

description: International climate conferences like the COP31 climate summit, now in its second week, tend to focus on the role of individual countries.
title: Large companies can still fall short on their climate commitments. Here's what must change

description: Over the past 800,000 years, Earth's history has been marked by dramatic shifts in climate, swinging from warm periods to cold, when large ice sheets covered much of the Northern Hemisphere and sea ice greatly expanded. The transition between the two climates is paced by the Earth's orbit with respect to the sun, but changes in the amount of carbon dioxide (CO2), a greenhouse gas, also affect global temperatures. By understanding how CO2 is exchanged between the atmosphere and the ocean, scientists hope to apply that knowledge to future climate scenarios.
title: How does ocean carbon sequestration change under different glacial conditions?

description: As global warming intensifies, scientists are exploring ways to reduce carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions. One emerging approach being explored in environmental research is carbon capture and storage (CCS), which involves capturing CO₂ and storing it deep underground, away from the atmosphere. In this context, researchers at the Indian Institute of Technology Gandhinagar (IITGN) have investigated ancient volcanic rocks in Maharashtra to assess their suitability for this purpose.
title: Lava flows studied for their carbon dioxide storage potential

description: Although lakes cover less than 2% of Earth's surface, they play a key role in regulating global carbon, nutrient and biodiversity dynamics.
title: Records from 2,000 lakes reveal ecological changes moving increasingly in sync

description: A 2026 Strategic Management Journal study finds that successful generative AI collaboration in expert work depends on how organizations integrate fundamentally different forms of human and AI knowledge.
title: New research shows why human–AI collaboration requires more than task allocation

description: Gold nanoclusters, composed of a small number of gold atoms, can exhibit optical, electronic and catalytic properties distinct from those of bulk gold. One intriguing family consists of carbon-centered gold(I) clusters, in which a carbon atom is surrounded by several gold atoms. Unlike the familiar four-coordinate carbon in methane, the central carbon in these clusters can be coordinated by five or even six gold atoms.
title: Unraveling bonding evolution in carbon-centered gold(I) clusters

description: NASA's Curiosity rover has been collecting data about Mars' thin, carbon dioxide–rich atmosphere since 2012. Now, a study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences has analyzed over a decade of this data to determine whether the daily and seasonal changes in Mars' atmosphere could be explained by known processes, including the freezing and release of carbon dioxide at its poles. What they found suggests a process involving water either attached to soil grains or in extremely thin, liquid-like films at the surface.
title: Over a decade of atmospheric data from NASA's Curiosity rover hints at small amounts of surface water on Mars

description: The acidity of tissues can provide important clues about a disease. Tumors and inflamed tissues often become more acidic than their surroundings because of changes in cellular metabolism. Measuring these pH variations could help researchers understand disease progression, identify abnormal tissue environments and evaluate treatment responses. However, detecting small pH differences inside the body remains challenging because magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) signals are affected by the concentration of the imaging agent used.
title: New nanoparticle MRI probe enables quantitative pH imaging

description: We rely on satellites every day for communications, weather forecasts and security, and more than 13,000 are currently circling the planet in low Earth orbit. But they could be more vulnerable than previously thought. Researchers have found that a single nuclear explosion in space could disable almost all of them.
title: How one nuclear blast could cripple nearly every satellite in low Earth orbit

description: Several years ago, a researcher from Kyoto University was conducting fieldwork in Borneo in an effort to understand why certain primates frequently choose trees along rivers as sleeping sites. Among other potential hypotheses, he wondered whether there were fewer mosquitoes along riverbanks, allowing primates to sleep more comfortably. This question soon motivated him and his team of researchers to investigate how mosquito abundance varies between riverbanks and inland forests.
title: Borneo forest survey reveals how mosquito abundance varies with river distance and height

description: The global shift toward cleaner energy raises a difficult financial question: Are fossil-fuel companies worth more than they should be because investors have not fully accounted for the risks of climate change and stronger climate policies?
title: The carbon bubble question: How much are fossil-fuel companies really at risk?

description: Two observers can start with the same description of a quantum system, follow the same probability rules and still disagree about the chance of the same outcome—even while being certain of each other's assessments.
title: Quantum observers can 'agree to disagree,' but within limits, new theorem shows

description: A working quarry isn't a pretty sight. Dust and bare rock, deep cuts into a hillside that appear like steps made for a giant. Nothing grows here, or so you would assume.
title: Small life, big job: Enlisting microbes to fight climate change

description: Astronomers have measured the orbit, masses and distance of a pair of small, active stars with extraordinary precision, using the U.S. National Science Foundation's Very Long Baseline Array (NSF VLBA), operated by the U.S. National Science Foundation National Radio Astronomy Observatory (NSF NRAO). The observations provide a remarkably detailed picture of DG CVn, a binary system in which two red dwarf stars orbit each other about 59 light-years from Earth.
title: Astronomers track a flaring dwarf-star duo with exceptional precision

description: In response to Alan Milburn's landmark review of England's NEET crisis—nearly 1 million young people ages 16–24 in the U.K. are not in education, employment or training—Prime Minister Andy Burnham has promised a "whole-childhood approach."
title: We know which young people are most likely to end up NEET in England—but not why

description: New research has shown that liming soil to improve its pH buffering capacity could help plant roots survive heat waves and maintain crop productivity under high temperatures.
title: Liming soil could help protect crops during extreme heat waves

description: As adults, we may take for granted what we know about numbers and how we arrived at this knowledge—for example, when comparing item prices to get the best deals or getting to appointments on time.
title: Building children's numeracy foundations involves more than 1, 2, 3

description: Scientists have revealed how a major pest of tea crops can escape the tea plant's natural catechin defense mechanisms. The research, published in eLife provides convincing evidence that links an enzyme, DOG15, with the ability of a spider mite to adapt to and overcome the catechin-based defenses of tea.
title: Pest mite overcomes catechin defenses in tea crops through a gene acquired from fungi

description: The holiday season is a time for gatherings with family and friends—as well as for less festive but necessary duties: organizing, preparing for and cleaning up after these gatherings. These are examples of service tasks that, according to previous research, women and girls are expected to perform.
title: Whom do we expect to put others ahead of themselves: Boys or girls? New study has surprising, and unsurprising, answers

description: From "three-strikes" laws to longer prison sentences, harsher penalties are imposed in the hope they'll reduce crime. But decades of research show that increasing punishment often does surprisingly little. What if we're missing something crucial? New research from the University of California San Diego suggests one potentially overlooked reason: people's moral motivations for breaking the law in the first place.
title: Why punishment doesn't always prevent crime

description: A new supernova has been spotted in NGC 1433, a spiral galaxy about 50 million light-years away. That's pretty close for supernova observations, and it's an opportunity for detailed follow-up study. It's not a core-collapse supernova, in which a massive star burns through its fuel, collapses and explodes. It's a Type Ia supernova. That means it's happening in a binary star system, where the exploding star is a white dwarf.
title: This supernova is 50 million light-years away, but that's close enough for astronomers

description: Losing a member of the flock can create a ripple of disruption across parakeet society. But when a missing bird returns home after a prolonged absence, feathers will fly.
title: Parting is sweet sorrow for parakeets—but a reunion might be worse

description: A ruler turns length into a position on a scale. A thermometer converts temperature into the height of a liquid column. In each case, a physical quantity becomes easier to read because an instrument gives it a visible reference. We wanted to bring the same idea to light, whose properties are usually measured with separate optical components and then interpreted through additional data processing.
title: Meta-compass: An on-chip toolkit for visualizing optical spectrum and polarization

description: A theoretical study expands classic game-theory models of cooperation by allowing payoffs to change with available environmental capacity. Games such as the prisoner's dilemma help researchers explore how cooperation could have evolved in a world of limited resources.
title: Available space reshapes cooperation and survival in new game theory model

description: As of Oct. 30, the Sentinel-6B satellite has been calibrated to serve as the world's go-to data source on sea level rise. The satellite has now passed all its initial system checks to ensure that its data meet the strictest quality and accuracy standards. In January, it will become the reference satellite that other sea-level missions use to calibrate their data.
title: NASA, European sea level satellite prepped for new role

description: When our ancestors interbred with Neanderthals tens of thousands of years ago, we inherited genetic variants that are still affecting us today.
title: Neanderthal DNA linked to a key brain structure may lower the risk of schizophrenia

description: Industrially relevant cell lines include both direct production hosts for recombinant proteins, vaccines and viral vectors, and biomedical models that serve as references for host-cell engineering and comparative studies. These cell lines support the development and worldwide supply of recombinant therapeutics, viral vaccines and gene therapies.
title: New database iCellOmics integrates multiomics data for industrial cell lines

description: Ireland could become a key player in Europe's transition toward greater food security and sustainable agriculture, according to new research led by researchers from University College Cork (UCC) and Teagasc.
title: Climate change could turn Ireland into a key producer of high-protein crops

description: How much do you know about managing your finances? And how much do you "think" you know?
title: When it comes to money, knowing what you don't know matters

description: Researchers at the University of Oxford have found that so-called "jumping genes" are surprisingly often incorporated into the genetic messages made by cells in the fruit fly brain. In the examples studied, an average of almost one in five RNA messages contained sequence from a jumping gene.
title: Jumping genes may help build a more diverse brain, fruit fly study reveals

description: The Thanksgiving turkey may be the centerpiece of the holiday meal, but cooking it, along with all the sides and other dishes, can invite an unexpected guest: indoor air pollution.
title: Cooking Thanksgiving dinner could create an indoor air quality problem inside your home, expert says

description: In "Star Trek," characters use a technology called a replicator to produce any food item they can imagine out of thin air. While we don't have this same technology in real life, we can get close with 3D printing.
title: Will it flow? Simulating food inks for 3D printing

description: Accurate division of genetic material is critical for life and growth, and key to this is a protein structure called the kinetochore. Without this structure, the genetic material cannot be segregated equally into two daughter cells. However, challenges in discovering the exact molecular organization of the kinetochore in living cells have prevented researchers from understanding how these proteins work together to build it.
title: Researchers count kinetochore proteins in living cells using an improved fluorescence-based method

description: The diamondback terrapin is North America's only turtle species that lives exclusively in brackish coastal waters, such as salt marshes and estuaries. Its populations face threats from historical overharvesting and contemporary habitat loss, coastal development and accidental capture in crab traps.
title: Tiny parasite holds big clues to help protect threatened estuarine turtles

description: The Norwegian government proposed Tuesday to start developing salmon farms on the open sea, away from the fjords and coastal pens where they are causing growing environmental and ecological damage.
title: Norway aims to put salmon farms on open seas

description: Saline-alkaline soils make farming difficult by restricting plant growth and reducing access to essential nutrients. Finding environmentally friendly ways to help crops grow in these soils is an important challenge for sustainable agriculture. A new study suggests that an unlikely source of useful bacteria may be hiding inside earthworms.
title: Earthworm gut bacteria show promise for helping crops grow in salt-affected soil

description: Sitting here on the outskirts of our Milky Way galaxy, it's hard to imagine the galactic machinations that led to our Goldilocks spot around a very welcoming yellow dwarf star. But for decades, astronomers have suspected that the internal dynamics of massive galaxies like ours play an outsized role in regulating star formation.
title: Galaxy outflows likely regulate star formation at 'cosmic noon,' NASA's Webb reveals

description: Quantum light sources that emit light with special quantum properties, such as single photons, are critical for quantum photonic technologies, including quantum communication, computing and sensing. In this regard, monolayer tungsten diselenide (WSe₂), a two-dimensional (2D) semiconductor material, hosts localized emissive states that enable light emission with sharp or narrow line widths, meaning that the emitted light has a narrow range of photon energies. This sharp luminescence makes this material a promising candidate for implementing on-chip quantum light sources.
title: Nanogap architecture could help integrate quantum light sources onto chips

description: The bacterial pathogen Xoo causes bacterial blight disease in rice plants that leads to substantial yield losses. Researchers from Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf (HHU) have published two advances on the infection mechanisms of the pathogen in the scientific journals Phytopathology and BMC Microbiology. They established that it is unlikely that the infection spreads from the roots to shoots via contaminated water and discovered that the bacterial cells assume multicellular forms to penetrate the leaf interior from the xylem network.
title: New findings reveal how rice blight spreads within plants and where it may stall

description: Researchers at Université Laval have described a new species of parasitic wasp from Quebec. The wasp, named Gonatopus quebecensis, develops on a leafhopper that spreads plant diseases in North American agriculture. The findings are published in the open-access journal ZooKeys.
title: Newly identified Quebec wasp attacks leafhoppers that spread crop diseases

description: Ever wandered through a field of plants and observed how their heights are relatively uniform? In nature, this is partly due to plants' ability to sense their neighbors through light receptors and shade-avoidance responses. When a lower ratio of red to far-red (FR) light is detected due to the presence of neighboring plants, plants elongate their stems to compete for light.
title: The color of uniformity: Far-red light effects on plant growth

description: How did the rich biodiversity in the tropics originally emerge? One traditional explanation is that tropical regions have provided species with favorable habitats for millions of years. While, for example, Europe's flora and fauna have been subjected to repeated ice ages, many ancient evolutionary lineages have persisted for a long time in the tropics.
title: Species in tropical rainforests may be surprisingly young with emergence linked to geological upheavals

description: The world has binding international agreements to protect the atmosphere, biodiversity and the high seas. But soil—an estimated US$325 trillion (A$473 trillion) natural asset that sustains life on Earth—has no dedicated international treaty.
title: The world's soil is worth US$325 trillion: Why isn't it protected?

description: Massive stellar companions can be difficult to detect because they emit little visible light or show no obvious signs of accretion. Their gravitational pull, however, can be traced through the motion of nearby stars. In pulsating stars, regular brightness variations act as natural clocks, offering a way to find these hidden objects.
title: Stellar pulsations reveal hidden 1.8-solar-mass companion

description: Researchers from the University of York will urge global action to tackle the growing threat of pharmaceuticals contaminating rivers and seas at a major United Nations conference in Geneva.
title: Scientists take global fight against pharmaceutical pollution to landmark UN summit

description: Quantum technologies, devices that can process, store or collect information leveraging the laws of quantum mechanics, could potentially outperform their classical counterparts on some tasks. Yet these devices are highly sensitive to changes or disturbances in their surrounding environment, which can disrupt quantum effects and lead to errors.
title: Team extends a qubit's lifetime, correcting errors without measuring them

description: New Strategic Management Journal research shows how founding relationships can shape firms long after the original partnership fades. Kunyuan Qiao, Shon R. Hiatt and Wesley D. Sine examine South American airlines founded in 10 countries between 1919 and 1984 and show that founding partners can leave two very different strategic legacies.
title: Airlines across 10 countries reveal how founding partners leave lasting assets and liabilities

description: Elementary particles and the forces governing their interactions are described by relativistic quantum field theory, in which symmetry serves as a fundamental guiding principle. For more than half a century, the possible symmetries of such theories were believed to be restricted by the Coleman–Mandula theorem and its supersymmetric extension, the Haag–Łopuszański–Sohnius theorem.
title: New theoretical framework free of ghostlike instabilities expands the possibilities of symmetry in particle physics

description: The argument for school cellphone bans is simple: Phones offer endless distraction. Take them away and students can focus on classwork, engage with peers and, ultimately, learn more.
title: Do school phone bans help students learn? So far, gains are 'modest'

description: The Bombay duck (Harpadon nehereus) is a small marine fish that lives in the northern Indian Ocean and western Pacific, including the East China Sea. For many years, fisheries in the East China Sea caught very few Bombay ducks.
title: DNA offers clues to the Bombay duck's rise in the East China Sea

description: Can you tell the difference between a scam text and a real one?
title: Account suspension. Verify now: The language of phishing

description: Discussions of legislative policies that promote fairer workplaces, such as employment nondiscrimination acts (ENDAs), have often revolved around their social and cultural merits, but recent scholarship has suggested they can lead to a wide range of broader economic benefits as well, including reducing turnover rates and increasing productivity and innovation.
title: Employment nondiscrimination acts led to reductions in manufacturing waste

description: Coupons promise savings, but not every shopper sees them as clear-cut bargains. For some consumers, such discounts may lead them to ask, "Where's the catch?"
title: Why some shoppers skip coupons—even when they offer a deal

description: A variety of interconnected risks—rooted in geopolitics, technology and the environment—are rising and converging on global supply chains. Within companies, the immediate result has been a shift in mindset.
title: Companies may not be laser-focused on supply chain risk—but lenders are

description: To estimate the Milky Way's mass, astronomers need to track the movements of stars and smaller satellite galaxies under its gravitational pull. The faster these objects travel at a given distance, the more mass is needed to hold them in place. For some time, these measurements have shown that most of our galaxy's mass can't be accounted for by the stars and gas we can see. However, they have also produced estimates that differ widely.
title: DESI weighs the Milky Way more precisely than ever

description: A Japanese probe that returned precious asteroid dust to Earth six years ago has changed course in its extended mission, officials said Tuesday, citing issues in its aging engines.
title: Japan space probe changes target over engine trouble

description: New research from the University of St Andrews, in collaboration with the University of Copenhagen, the North Coast Cetacean Society and Fisheries and Oceans Canada, has sequenced a whole whale genome using samples of "whale snot" collected by small drones off the coast of British Columbia—a world first.
title: Humpback whale snot unlocks whole-genome sequencing without invasive sampling

description: Dark matter continues to evade direct detection. Its slower-moving particles might leave signals too faint for detectors to register, yet be more easily captured by planets and stars. As they accumulate inside these bodies, they could produce effects that existing instruments would allow us to search for.
title: The sun, Earth, Jupiter and white dwarfs: Potential traps for dark matter
